title: Prove: Sum of Triangle Angles = 180°

statement.text: Prove that the sum of the interior angles of any triangle equals 180 degrees.

objectives: Use parallel line properties in proofs
Construct auxiliary lines to aid proofs

currentState.description: We have a triangle ABC with angles α, β, and γ. We need to prove:

prompt.question: What's a good first step for this proof?
prompt.hint: Consider adding a construction that creates parallel lines.

options.text: Draw a line through vertex A parallel to side BC
Measure all three angles with a protractor to show they sum to 180°
Start by assuming the sum equals 180° and work backwards

correct.explanation: Excellent! Drawing a line parallel to BC through A is a classic construction for this proof. It will allow us to use properties of parallel lines and transversals.
correct.insight: Strategic auxiliary lines are powerful tools in geometric proofs.

incorrect.1: Measuring with a protractor shows it's true for one triangle, but doesn't prove it's true for ALL triangles. We need a general proof.
incorrect.2: That's circular reasoning. We can't assume what we're trying to prove. We need to build up to the conclusion.

resultState.description: We've drawn line DE through vertex A, parallel to BC:

currentState.description: We have triangle ABC with line DE through A parallel to BC:

prompt.question: What angle relationship can we identify now?
prompt.hint: Look at the angles formed where the transversals cross the parallel lines.

options.text: Identify alternate interior angles: angle ABC = angle DAB, and angle ACB = angle EAC
All angles are equal because the lines are parallel
The parallel lines don't create any useful angle relationships

correct.explanation: Perfect! When a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are equal. So angle β (at B) equals angle DAB, and angle γ (at C) equals angle EAC.
correct.insight: Alternate interior angles theorem is key to many geometric proofs.

incorrect.1: Not all angles are equal. Only specific pairs of angles (alternate interior angles) are equal when formed by parallel lines and a transversal.
incorrect.2: On the contrary! Parallel lines create very useful angle relationships, specifically alternate interior angles.

prompt.question: Looking at point A, what do we notice about angles DAB, BAC, and EAC?
prompt.hint: Consider how these three angles are arranged at point A.

options.text: These three angles form a straight line at point A, so they sum to 180°
These angles form a triangle, so they sum to 180°

correct.explanation: Exactly! The three angles DAB, BAC (which is α), and EAC all meet at point A and together form line DE, which is a straight line. Angles on a straight line sum to 180°.
correct.insight: Angles that form a straight line always sum to 180° (supplementary angles).

incorrect.1: The angles are at a point on a line, not forming a triangle. They lie along the straight line DE.
incorrect.2: These angles are generally not all equal. They represent the three different angles of the triangle.

resultState.description: Angles on line DE at point A:
equations: angle DAB + angle BAC + angle EAC = 180°

prompt.question: How do we complete the proof?
prompt.hint: Substitute the equal angles we found earlier.

options.text: Substitute: β + α + γ = 180°, proving the sum of triangle angles is 180°
We need to measure the angles to complete the proof
Use the Pythagorean theorem to verify

correct.explanation: Perfect! Since angle DAB = β and angle EAC = γ, we can substitute into our equation: β + α + γ = 180°. This proves that the three interior angles of triangle ABC sum to 180°!
correct.insight: This proof works for ANY triangle because we only used general properties of parallel lines and straight angles.

incorrect.1: No measurement needed! We've used logical reasoning and geometric properties to prove this for all triangles.
incorrect.2: The Pythagorean theorem is about side lengths in right triangles, not about angle sums. It's not relevant here.

keyInsights: Auxiliary constructions (like parallel lines) can reveal hidden relationships
Alternate interior angles are equal when formed by parallel lines and a transversal
Angles on a straight line sum to 180°
This proof works for ANY triangle, not just specific examples
summary.fullSolution: Draw a line through vertex A parallel to BC. By alternate interior angles, the base angles of the triangle equal the angles formed on the line at A. Since these angles form a straight line, they sum to 180°.
